summary: Ticket-facing coverage is largely present: fake HTTP tests cover release→import, content/search, delay, wrong ids, reset, revision cleanup, and controls; real adapters get a combined happy path plus import-FAILED. Remaining gaps are the verifyRevision document-count filter (only implicit), content-control failures never driven through the Pinpoint adapter against the fake, and a thin combined failure matrix beyond import FAILED.

findings.summary: verifyRevision’s new document-count filter has no focused unit test.
findings.rationale: Combined fixtures now carry document-count plus Pinpoint content/search; verifyRevision strips document-count so it no longer throws. Existing Pinpoint unit tests still only assert prepare refuses document-count for direct import, and observation-only stubs never pass a mixed fixture through verifyRevision. The untracked combined pipeline is the sole proof — a regression that re-rejects document-count here would stay green in pinpoint/adapter.test.ts.

findings.summary: failNextContent/corruptNextContent are never exercised through the Pinpoint adapter against the fake.
findings.rationale: The new one-shot controls are asserted only via raw fetch (status/body). Stub-based verify tests cover similar missing/wrong-publication failures, and adapter+fake happy paths cover success, but nothing shows createPinpointAdapter.verify or verifyRevision failing when the fake injects ERR4004 or a mismatched publication.id — the seam the ticket’s missing/corrupt-content cases were meant to harden.

findings.summary: Real-adapter combined suite only covers happy path and import FAILED.
findings.rationale: Ticket asked for missing/corrupt content, delayed search, wrong publication/revision, interrupted/reset, and cleanup, plus integration with actual adapters. Those failure modes live in fake/server.test.ts (HTTP), while combined-fake-pipeline.test.ts only runs success and failNextImport. RunEngine + both adapters never see COMPLETED-then-verify-fails, searchVisibilityDelayMs vs adapter polling, or cleanup of a release-driven import.

findings.summary: Publication DELETE cleanup of release-driven imports is untested.
findings.rationale: New imports.delete in deletePublication mirrors the tested revision-DELETE path, but no case deletes the publication and asserts the import/content surface is gone. A miss here could leave completed imports serving content after publication teardown.
